title: harness-autopilot: let projects declare additional domain-specific review skills

pipelineStages.summary: Spec: optional review.additionalSkills[] config seam; extra reviewers run at BOTH REVIEW and FINAL_REVIEW alongside the mandatory harness-code-reviewer; empty/absent = no regression; unresolvable skill = failure not skip.
4-task TDD plan: schema field (test-first), SKILL.md wiring (prose-contract test-first), docs, validate.
TDD implementation: additionalSkills added to ReviewConfigSchema + autopilot SKILL.md wired at REVIEW and FINAL_REVIEW + configuration.md updated.
Self-review + code-review pass; schema + prose-contract tests green; no regression to single-reviewer path.

assumptions: GENERALIZED: the one-off review.additionalSkills field is removed and superseded by a general cross-skill skillHooks framework (shape = top-level map keyed by skill-name -> event-string -> hook-entry[]); the review case is now skillHooks["harness-autopilot"]["after:REVIEW"] + ["after:FINAL_REVIEW"]

shared resolver in @harness-engineering/core (packages/core/src/hooks/skill-lifecycle.ts): resolveSkillHooks(config, skillName, event) -> NormalizedHook[]; defaultBlocking(event) = true at review/verify events else false, per-entry blocking overrides

hook entry is a bare skill-name string OR a discriminated union on type: skill (subagent dispatch), prompt (mechanically append text to the persona prompt; never blocks), command (mechanically run a shell command via the command-runner; deterministic, no LLM)

event-key grammar = ^(before|after|on):[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ — before:/after:<phase>, before:run/after:run (covers single-shot phase-less skills), and on:<event> lifecycle hooks (on:failure proven in autopilot)

hook input-context contract centralized in core (hook-context.ts): command hooks get HARNESS_* env vars + JSON stdin (absent values unset, not empty); skill hooks get the same context in the subagent brief; prompt is static text; on:failure sets HARNESS_FAILURE_REASON
enabled toggle (default true) on all three object kinds parks a hook without deleting it — a disabled hook is skipped, never a hard halt

hard-halt policy: unresolvable/undispatchable skill = hard halt (false-green protection, recorded in .harness/failures.md, not overridable); command that cannot be spawned = hard halt; command that ran and exited non-zero = a normal blocking finding; prompt never blocks/halts
empty/absent skillHooks preserves today's exact single-reviewer behavior — no regression

proven on autopilot at 2 states (after:REVIEW + after:FINAL_REVIEW migrated, before:EXECUTE for non-review generality) across all three kinds, plus on:failure; harness-code-review is the second consumer (after:mechanical), resolver-level proof

RESERVED v2 (documented, not implemented): per-iteration granularity (after:EXECUTE:task, after:dispatch:item), a "*" wildcard outer key, and {{token}} prompt templating; conditional scoping is achievable today by a command self-gating on $HARNESS_CHANGED_FILES
autopilot/code-review are prose-driven skills, so dispatch wiring lives in their SKILL.md; the schema + resolver + context helpers are the TypeScript code surface
